candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the uploaded NAR's META-INF/MANIFEST.MF attributes Nar-Group, Nar-Id and Nar-Version (read by NarBundleExtractor.getBundleCoordinate, only non-blank-checked by BundleIdentifier). Upload is a normal authenticated multipart POST to /buckets/{bucketId}/bundles/{bundleType} (BucketBundleResource.createExtensionBundleVersion) gated only by WRITE policy on /buckets/{bucketId}; the destructive sink is reached by DELETE /buckets/{bucketId}/bundles/{bundleId} (BundleResource.deleteBundle -> StandardServiceFacade.deleteBundle -> StandardExtensionService.deleteBundle -> deleteAllBundleVersions) gated by DELETE/READ policy on the bucket. A crafted NAR must also carry a parseable Build-Timestamp attribute (NarBundleExtractor.getBuildInfo), which the uploader supplies.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that coordinates are validated elsewhere: BundleIdentifier (non-blank only), Bundle.groupId/artifactId (@NotBlank only), BundleVersionMetadata.version (@NotBlank only), StandardBundleCoordinate/StandardBundleVersionCoordinate (Validate.notBlank only) — none rejects '.'/'..'. Checked FileUtils.sanitizeFilename's INVALID_CHARS list (lines 394-425): it includes /, \, control characters, : * ? " < > | and space, so '..' passes unchanged. Checked that no canonical-path/startsWith containment guard exists in the persistence provider or service layer, and that the minifi-c2 cache does use an explicit parent-equality check (FileSystemConfigurationCache.resolveChildAndVerifyParent) while this provider does not. Confirmed the delete sink's bundleDir.exists() precondition can be satisfied because the upload path's ensureDirectoryExistAndCanReadAndWrite mkdirs creates the <bucketUuid> directory first. Confirmed MiNiFi-CPP extractor is unimplemented (only NIFI_NAR path is reachable) and that the file name built from artifactId+'-'+version cannot itself contain separators (limits the write primitive to planting files with constrained names, not overwriting arbitrary file names).
candidates.impact: Authenticated path traversal/arbitrary location file write and, via cleanDirectory, recursive deletion of files outside the intended extension bundle storage directory. With the default ./extension_bundles layout, deleting a crafted bundle recursively wipes the contents of the NiFi Registry home (configuration, H2 database/flow storage, logs, etc.), destroying registry state and availability; the write side lets an uploader place attacker-controlled file content at an attacker-influenced directory above the storage root. This is a server-side integrity/availability compromise caused by one low-privileged registry user, not a client-side or self-inflicted action.
candidates.prerequisites: NiFi Registry with the default file-based extension bundle persistence provider (conf/providers.xml: 'Extension Bundle Storage Directory'=./extension_bundles, so the storage parent is the registry working/home directory) and an authenticated user holding write (and, for the worst impact, delete) permission on at least one bucket. No unauthenticated access is required. The write-path filename component cannot contain path separators because sanitize replaces them, so the write primitive plants an oddly-named file; the recursive cleanDirectory reached via the same coordinates is the severe consequence.
candidates.root_cause: NAR MANIFEST attributes Nar-Group/Nar-Id/Nar-Version are stored as the bundle's groupId/artifactId/version with only non-blank validation (BundleIdentifier.validateNotBlank, Bundle @NotBlank, BundleVersionMetadata @NotBlank). FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider builds filesystem paths by concatenating sanitize(bucketId)+"/"+sanitize(groupId)+"/"+sanitize(artifactId)[+"/"+sanitize(version)] and resolving with new File(storage, ...). sanitize() only delegates to FileUtils.sanitizeFilename (replaces /, \, control chars, : * ? " < > | and space) plus trim/lowercase, so a value of ".." is passed through unchanged. No path normalization/containment check (e.g., canonical path startsWith storage root, or reject "."/".." segments) exists before the write/read/delete sinks. The write sink writes attacker-controlled bytes to that path, and deleteAllBundleVersions calls org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils.cleanDirectory(bundleDir), which recursively deletes all contents of the resolved directory (which can be the parent/grandparent of the storage directory).
candidates.title: Path traversal via NiFi Registry extension-bundle coordinates allows writes and recursive deletion outside the bundle storage directory
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker uploads a crafted NAR with Nar-Group='..', Nar-Id='..', Nar-Version='..' (or similar dotted values). 2) StandardExtensionService.createBundleVersion (lines 195-264) takes groupId/artifactId/version from the extracted BundleIdentifier, creates/uses a BundleEntity without path validation (getOrCreateExtensionBundle validates only @NotBlank), then persistBundleVersionContent (lines 388-416) builds StandardBundleVersionCoordinate. 3) FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider.createBundleVersion/saveOrUpdateBundleVersion (lines 92-119) computes getBundleVersionDirectory (lines 213-220) = new File(bundleStorageDir, sanitize(bucketId)+'/'+sanitize(groupId)+'/'+sanitize(artifactId)+'/'+sanitize(version)); with '..' segments this resolves above bundleStorageDir, ensureDirectoryExistAndCanReadAndWrite mkdirs it, and FileOutputStream writes attacker content to getBundleFile (lines 222-231). 4) On DELETE, StandardExtensionService.deleteBundle (lines 462-481) builds a StandardBundleCoordinate from the same stored group/artifact values and calls deleteAllBundleVersions; getBundleDirectory (lines 205-211) yields bundleStorageDir/<uuid>/../.., which exists (the <uuid> directory was created during upload), and line 169 calls org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils.cleanDirectory(bundleDir) — recursively deleting every file/subdirectory in the resolved ancestor directory (default: contents of the registry home such as conf/ and database/). 5) The same coordinate values are also used by getBundleVersionContent (lines 121-139) for reads and by deleteBundleVersion (lines 141-157) for single-file deletion.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no filesystem/database behavior was run-time confirmed; the finding is source-derived. The assumption that the metadata DB accepts and returns '..' coordinates rests on the validation annotations above, not on a live database. Impact for non-default provider layouts (e.g., S3 provider, storage dir outside the installation) is correspondingly different. It is also not verified whether this snapshot is exactly the parent of an upstream security fix, so I do not claim a CVE mapping.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') (also CWE-73, CWE-668)

coverage_summary: get_source_scope: 7,852 source files in scope, 31 excluded by sensitive-name/path filter, binary-like files refused/skipped, and the snapshot contains main sources only (no src/test trees). get_relation_scope: complete syntactic index over all 7,852 files (83,557 symbols, 242,172 call rows, 181,674 edges, 2,940 facts), explicitly not SAST and not proof of reachability or data flow; build/tests were not run and no findings/oracle were loaded. I inspected source text (not just index labels) in: NiFi Registry extension-bundle upload/delete/persistence chain and related validation/coordinate classes; nifi-web-security OIDC/SAML/JWT/CSRF/proxied-entities/request filters; nifi-web-api authorization guards and AccessResource/OIDCAccessResource; nifi-framework authorization and swap/queue code (sampled); MiNiFi C2 client, minifi-framework C2 command helpers, minifi-c2 service/security/cache; bootstrap ShellRunner and command runners; standard-processors FTP virtual filesystem, UnpackContent, ExecuteProcess/StreamCommand, lookup/SQL services (sampled). Processor bundles and UI JavaScript were only lightly sampled.
limitations: Static review only: no code, tests, scanners, or payloads were executed; no runtime confirmation exists for any candidate.
No upstream history/diff is available in the snapshot, so I cannot confirm whether the missing coordinate validation is an upstream bug or an intentionally reverted fix, nor map it to a CVE.

The relation index is syntactic (calls/containment/inheritance hints) and does not prove runtime reachability or data flow; every cited edge was re-verified in source text, but no complete data-flow analysis was performed.
The snapshot omits test sources, so expected-behavior tests for the persistence provider were unavailable.

Coverage is not exhaustive across all 7,852 files: third-party-style processor bundles, large DTO/factory classes, and UI JavaScript were sampled rather than fully audited; findings in uninspected areas cannot be ruled out.
Exploitability of the selected candidate depends on deployment configuration (file-based bundle provider path, granted registry bucket policies) which cannot be validated from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: NiFi core OIDC state validation: OIDCAccessResource.checkOidcState (nifi-web-api OIDCAccessResource.java:501-512) logs/forwards a message but does not throw/return on a state mismatch, so oidcCallback/oidcLogoutCallback continue into token exchange; the sibling NiFi Registry implementation (AccessResource.validateOIDCState, lines 1010-1025) throws instead.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible login-CSRF/OIDC state-bypass weakness, but exploitation requires the victim to have an in-progress OIDC request cookie plus an attacker-obtained authorization code, and the security impact is indirect; the source evidence of 'missing abort' is weaker than the registry traversal's concrete file sinks, so it was not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: MiNiFi Java C2 asset path traversal: UpdateAssetCommandHelper.assetUpdatePrecondition/assetPersistFunction (minifi-framework-core UpdateAssetCommandHelper.java:47-68) join the C2-supplied assetFileName to the asset directory with no normalization or containment check (Files.write/deleteIfExists on the result).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only from a C2 command; the C2 server is the agent's trusted control plane, so the attacker model (compromised/malicious C2 endpoint) is weaker than the authenticated-registry-user model of the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: ContentLengthFilter read-limit bypass: LimitedContentLengthRequest (nifi-web-security ContentLengthFilter.java:140-184) overrides only ServletInputStream.read() and counts bytes only there, so callers using read(byte[],int,int) or transferTo can exceed maxContentLength when the declared Content-Length is under the limit.
rejected_leads.reason: Appears to be a hardening/DoS gap rather than a demonstrated exploitable vulnerability in the reviewed code paths, and no concrete downstream unbounded-read impact was traced.

rejected_leads.lead: Host-header-derived redirects: WebUtils.determineProxiedHost/RequestUriBuilder (nifi-web-utils) prefer X-ProxyHost/X-Forwarded-Host when building login/logout redirect URIs.
rejected_leads.reason: Proxied-header trust is a documented deployment model and no unvalidated cross-origin redirect with security consequence was confirmed; left as an unconfirmed lead.

summary: Repo is Apache NiFi/MiNiFi/Registry 1.20.0-SNAPSHOT (7,852 files; main sources only, no tests). Reviewed security-critical areas (nifi-registry bundle persistence + extension upload/delete REST path, nifi-web-security OIDC/SAML/JWT/CSRF/proxied-entity and request filters, framework authorization guards, minifi C2 client/server, bootstrap shell handling, standard processors' FTP/Unpack/SQL paths) using only source text plus the syntactic relation index. Strongest source-evidenced issue: an authenticated user with write access to a NiFi Registry bucket can upload a NAR whose MANIFEST coordinates (Nar-Group/Nar-Id/Nar-Version) are only checked for non-blankness; "."/".." values survive the sanitize step and are joined into filesystem paths without any containment check. This yields attacker-directed writes outside the configured Extension Bundle Storage Directory and, worse, a DELETE of the bundle recurses the same path into org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils.cleanDirectory, wiping the contents of an ancestor directory (by default the registry working directory exposing conf/, database/, logs/).
